title: Burst latency profiling toolkit and chaos hooks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for diagnosing short-duration (burst) tail-latency regressions in the serving runtime. Focus is on low-noise capture, portable flamegraph artifacts, and lightweight chaos hooks that reproduce scheduling and IO-induced bursts in CI. The goal: actionable traces that point to hot code paths and resource contention in the first 200ms–2s of a request.

Scope and assumptions:
- Targets: hosted inference and Dedicated worker pools (GPU + CPU path).
- We care about short bursts (single-request tail spikes) rather than sustained throughput saturation.
- Minimal production impact: collector agent runs in local CI or can be toggled on dedicated canaries. Avoid heavy instrumentation on prod control planes.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 mins):
1) Reproduce locally: pick a failing request from stderr / trace sample. Save prompt+headers to repro/request.json.
2) Run lightweight latency prober against same model variant to capture distribution (5k samples, p50/p95/p99). Command: tools/latency-prober --model x --seq 512 --concurrency 1 --count 5000 --out metrics.csv
3) If p99 > expected, trigger burst capture job (see Capture procedures).

Capture procedures (ordered by intrusiveness):
A. In-process async stack sampler (lowest overhead):
- Start serving with SAMPLER=1 env (runtime feature flag) which periodically writes user-space stacks to /tmp/ss-snap-*.raw.
- Run repro workload for 2x observed burst window.
- Collapse stacks into folded format and produce flamegraph.svg: 
  - tools/fold-stacks.py /tmp/ss-snap-*.raw > folded.txt
  - FlameGraph/stackcollapse.pl folded.txt > folded.collapsed
  - FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl folded.collapsed > flamegraph.svg
Notes: sampler resolution defaults to 5ms; increase to 1ms when investigating sub-50ms hotspots but beware CPU overhead.

B. eBPF perf events (kernel + user stacks, higher fidelity):
- Use our eBPF wrapper script to collect samples and capture kernel+user stacks for pid <pid>:
  - scripts/ebpf-capture.sh --pid 12345 --duration 20s --freq 4000 --out /tmp/ebpf-burst.raw
- Convert to folded format: scripts/ebpf-unwrap.py /tmp/ebpf-burst.raw > ebpf.folded
- Generate flamegraph as above.
Notes: on GKE nodes with restricted CAP_SYS_ADMIN, run from a privileged job or on a debug node.

C. Perf + unwind + heap profiler (heavy, post-mortem):
- perf record -F 4999 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 20
- perf script | FlameGraph/stackcollapse-perf.pl > perf.collapsed
- FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl perf.collapsed > perf-flame.svg
Use when eBPF not available. Larger disk/CPU footprint.

What to capture besides stacks:
- KV-cache telemetry span for each request: kvcache.hits|misses counts, timestamps. Export with --trace-kvcache flag to trace collector.
- GPU metrics: nvml sampling (util, mem, ecc) at 50ms. tools/gpu-sampler --pid <pid> --freq 50 --out gpu.csv
- CPU steal/softirq: node exporter + short scrape (1s) around repro window.
- Tracing headers: request-id, deployment-version, model-variant, route. Include these in samples to filter artifacts.

CI perf job: burst-latency-smoke
- Job triggers: nightly + on PRs touching runtime/* and kvcache/*; also triggered manually via Linear link.
- Job steps (CI YAML snippet paraphrased):
  1) spin up docker runtime image with debug flags (DEBUG_PROFILE=1)
  2) start local trace-collector (lightweight) and mount /tmp/artifacts
  3) run synthetic burst harness: tools/burst-client --pattern sudden --n 1000 --concurrency 16 --seq 1024
  4) run ebpf-capture.sh during the 30s window
  5) produce flamegraphs and upload to artifacts store (S3 path prefix: s3://redwood-profiling/burst/${CI_JOB_ID}/)
- Artifact retention: keep last 30 runs; store p95/p99 latency CSV + flamegraph.svg + gpu.csv + collector.log

Chaos hooks (repro knobs to provoke bursts):
- Scheduler pause: ch-ctl pause-thread --pid <pid> --thread <tid> --duration 200ms (simulates GC/stop-the-world vibe)
- IO burst: tools/io-noise --target /dev/nvme0n1 --iops 40000 --duration 10s (simulate noisy neighbor disk writes)
- Network delay injection: tc qdisc add dev eth0 root netem delay 40ms 5ms distribution normal
- Memory pressure: tools/mem-press --target-pid <pid> --alloc 1G --hold 5s
Notes: attach these in dedicated debug canaries only (never on production control plane). Combine hooks to reproduce multi-dimensional contention.

Investigation heuristics (how to read artifacts):
- Single hot function frames near top of flame = CPU hotspot. Cross-check with source + recent PRs.
- Wide thin flames across many syscalls = scheduling or IO noise. Look at kernel frames and softirq stack.
- Long tail in user stacks with the same callsite but varying call-path = cache/locking contention. Correlate with kvcache hit/miss spans.
- GPU stalls visible as user threads idle while nvml shows GPU queue depth high = batching/queueing problem or GPU-side memory thrashing.

Example debugging scenario (short):
- Symptom: p99 jumps to 1.6s for model-variant v2 only during peak minute.
- Captures: eBPF flamegraph shows long waits in futex_wait for ~300ms inside kv::lookup; kvcache misses spike in collector.log; nvml shows high GPU utilization.
- Hypothesis: kvcache eviction thrashing causes CPU waits which delay dispatch to GPU, creating request pileups.
- Remediation steps: increase kvcache size in config (kvcache.items=2M), enable async kvcache lookup (feature flag async-kvcache=true), and deploy canary. Re-run CI burst job to validate.

Common pitfalls and how to avoid them:
- Over-instrumenting in prod: enable sampling at low resolution and short windows; prefer debug canaries.
- Ignoring clock skew: use monotonic timestamps in all samplers and collector—tools use rdtsc-safe timestamping by default.
- Ambient noise in CI: pin CPUs, set GOMAXPROCS/OMP_NUM_THREADS to match expected worker count in test harness.

Commands and useful one-liners:
- Create folded stacks from eBPF raw and upload to S3:
  scripts/ebpf-unwrap.py /tmp/ebpf-burst.raw > /tmp/ebpf.folded && 
  FlameGraph/flamegraph.pl /tmp/ebpf.folded > /tmp/ebpf.svg && 
  aws s3 cp /tmp/ebpf.svg s3://redwood-profiling/burst/${CI_JOB_ID}/ebpf.svg
- Quick p99 check from CSV:
  awk -F"," '{arr[NR]=$5} END{n=NR; asort(arr); print arr[int(n*0.99)]}' metrics.csv

On-call runbook snippet (for SREs):
- If a customer reports intermittent latency spike:
  1) Check console per-route p95/p99 graphs and note timestamps.
  2) Pull trace-collector artifacts for the time window (s3 path convention).
  3) If no artifacts, trigger an adhoc capturing canary on the affected node pool (run debug image with SAMPLER=1 for 10m).
  4) Escalate to runtime team if flamegraph shows lock contention or syscalls; include top-5 frames and collector.log.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Integrate the ebpf-unwrap pipeline into the CI job to auto-annotate flame frames with source file:line using debug symbols. (OWNER: Ilya)
- Add GPU timeline overlay in flamegraph artifacts (sync nvml csv -> flame metadata). (OWNER: Hannah)
- Create a lightweight web UI to diff two flamegraphs and highlight frame deltas (spike vs baseline). Prototype under /tools/flame-diff/. (OWNER: Omar)

Notes to self / rough ideas (scratch):
- Could embed kvcache-per-key sampling to find hot keys causing thrash. Implement via sampling adaptor in trace-collector.
- Consider a short lived microbench that reproduces evictions with controlled TTLs rather than relying on heavy production sampling.

References and examples:
- FlameGraph toolkit: https://github.com/brendangregg/FlameGraph
- Internal PR: trace-collector instrumentation for kvcache spans: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-collector/pull/412
- Linear ticket for CI job: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PROF-89/ci-burst-latency-job

Appendix A: scripts inventory (path relative to repo root)
- scripts/ebpf-capture.sh  -- wrapper around bpftrace/tracee for quick captures
- scripts/ebpf-unwrap.py -- convert raw ebpf to folded stacks (adds annotation)
- tools/latency-prober -- synthetic client used in CI and local runs
- tools/burst-client -- patterned burst scenarios (sudden, ramp, jitter)
- tools/gpu-sampler -- nvml time series dumper
- tools/io-noise -- simple fio wrapper to generate disk bursts

Appendix B: sample flamegraph diagnostic template to paste in Slack:
- p99: 1.6s, window: 2025-02-26T16:12:10Z–16:17:30Z, model: gpt-redwood-7b-v2
- Top frames: kv::lookup::futex_wait(33%), request_dispatcher::enqueue(17%), tokio::io::read(12%)
- Attached: s3://redwood-profiling/burst/12345/ebpf.svg, gpu.csv, collector.log
- Initial hypothesis: kvcache eviction stalls causing dispatch pileup; recommended action: enable async-kvcache on canary and re-run burst job.

End of document.
